title: Black holes
text: A black hole is a place in space where gravity is so strong that nothing can escape from it, not even light. That is why we cannot see black holes directly: they are completely dark.

Most black holes form when a giant star dies. If a star were big enough, it would collapse at the end of its life and squeeze all its mass into a tiny space. In the center of our galaxy there is a supermassive black hole, four million times heavier than the Sun.

What would happen if you fell into a black hole? Scientists have a funny name for it: spaghettification. The gravity on your feet would be much stronger than on your head, so your body would be stretched like spaghetti.
Time also behaves strangely near a black hole. If you stayed close to one for an hour, many years would pass on Earth. When you came back, your friends would be much older than you.

In 2019 scientists published the first image of a black hole. It looked like a dark circle surrounded by a ring of fire. If we had better telescopes, we would probably discover many more secrets about these mysterious objects.

grammar.title: Grammar: the second conditional
grammar.rule: Use the second conditional for imaginary situations: If + past simple, would + verb. With the verb to be, we often use were for all people.
rows: If you fell, you would be stretched.
If you stayed, years would pass.
If I were an astronaut, I would go.
If we had telescopes, we would see more.
items: If you fell into a black hole, you ___ be stretched.
If you ___ near it for an hour, years would pass.
If I ___ an astronaut, I would go to space.
If we had better telescopes, we ___ discover more.
Your friends would be older if you ___ back.
